approval.cost: No listing or review fee is stated in the docs read (the Marketplace FAQ mentions developer payouts are processed monthly once the sum is at least $100; a payout threshold, not a fee)
approval.trigger: OAuth clients: no review or approval is described anywhere in the Zoho CRM developer docs; registration is instant self-service and external users in other organizations can authorize your client. (Absence-of-documentation finding, not an affirmative policy statement.) The optional Zoho Marketplace track is for CRM EXTENSIONS, not OAuth: publishing an extension privately needs no review (you get a shareable install URL), while listing publicly requires Zoho's review via the 'List your extension in the Zoho Marketplace' checkbox and submission form (status 'Waiting for approval').
approval.wait: Marketplace extension review: 'usually takes 24-48 hours' (stated in Zoho Marketplace help; the developer FAQ likewise says 48 hours). OAuth client approval: none exists

blockers.detail: Zoho runs separate DCs (US .com, EU .eu, IN .in, AU .com.au, JP .jp, CN .com.cn, SA .sa, CA zohocloud.ca). Registration, grant, and token calls must all happen in the user's DC (read location/accounts-server from the redirect) unless you enable Multi-DC, and 'each DC holds a unique client secret', so a DC-mismatched secret yields invalid_client.
blockers.howToClear: Route every call by the accounts-server value returned in the redirect, or enable Multi-DC and store the per-DC secrets.
blockers.title: Data-center fragmentation

blockers.detail: 'Max 20 refresh tokens per user': generating the 21st invalidates the first created, 'irrespective of whether the first refresh token is in use or not'. Every re-consent mints a NEW refresh token, so an integration that prompts re-authorization repeatedly can silently kill its own (or another session's) stored token. Related throttles: max 10 grant tokens per client ID in 10 minutes; max 10 access tokens from a refresh token in 10 minutes; max 15 active access tokens per refresh token (the 16th invalidates the oldest).
blockers.howToClear: Avoid gratuitous re-consents, reuse valid access tokens instead of minting new ones, and treat refresh-token invalidation as an expected failure mode.
blockers.title: The 20-refresh-token trap

blockers.detail: The Token Validity page says the grant token is 'a one-time use token and valid for three minutes, by default'; the Authorization Request page says 'valid only for two minutes'; the Access & Refresh Tokens error page says 'valid only for one minute in the redirection-based flow'.
blockers.howToClear: Exchange the code immediately on receipt; design for the shortest stated lifetime.
blockers.title: Grant-token lifetime is stated inconsistently (1, 2, or 3 minutes)

flavor.recommended: A Server-based Application client in the Zoho API Console, authorized with access_type=offline
flavor.why: The object is a client (the token docs also call it a 'connected app') registered in the Zoho API Console / Developer Console (api-console.zoho.com), issuing a Client ID and Client Secret. Zoho Accounts is the OAuth 2.0 server for all Zoho services. Server-based is 'chosen when your application is used by multiple users and requires user intervention during authorization'. Scopes are requested per authorization (not fixed at registration) and are granular (ZohoCRM.modules.ALL, ZohoCRM.users.READ, and per-module READ/CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/ALL). CRM has a real, open OAuth program: any user can register a client self-service and any Zoho user can authorize it.

humanMust: Register the client in the Zoho API Console (requires a Zoho account)
Optionally enable Multi-DC in the console (Settings) and manage the per-DC client secrets
name: Zoho CRM
nuances: access_type=online returns NO refresh token; forgetting access_type=offline means re-consent every hour. Refresh tokens 'do not expire until a user revokes them'.

Tokens are organization- and environment-specific: a grant is for one chosen org in one environment (Production/Sandbox/Developer), chosen by the user at consent; tokens from one cannot be used against another.

API calls use the nonstandard header scheme 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token}', not Bearer, despite token_type: Bearer in the token response. The token response returns api_domain, which is where API calls go.

Dummy homepage/redirect values are permitted at registration if you don't have a domain yet (per the SDK registration docs), but the runtime redirect_uri must exactly match the registered one (ERROR_invalid_redirect_uri otherwise).
Each access token is valid for one hour (expires_in 3600).
prerequisites: A Zoho account for the API Console
Client Name, Homepage URL, and Authorized Redirect URI(s)
A DC strategy: per-DC routing via accounts-server, or Multi-DC enabled

steps.detail: Zoho API Console: choose Server-based Application, enter Client Name, Homepage URL, and Authorized Redirect URI(s), click Create; receive Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Register a Server-based client

steps.detail: accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/auth?scope={scopes}&client_id={id}&response_type=code&access_type=offline&redirect_uri={uri} (use the user's DC host). The user logs in, picks the organization and environment the grant applies to if they have several, and Accepts or Rejects (error=access_denied on reject).
steps.title: Redirect the user to authorize (access_type=offline)

steps.detail: POST {accounts-server}/oauth/v2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, using the domain-specific accounts URL returned in the redirect (e.g. accounts.zoho.eu for EU users). Response: access_token, refresh_token, api_domain, token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600.
steps.title: Exchange the grant token immediately

steps.detail: Call the CRM API at the returned api_domain with header 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token}'. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the same DC's token endpoint before the 1-hour expiry; reuse valid access tokens rather than minting new ones (throttles apply).
steps.title: Call the API (Zoho-oauthtoken header); refresh hourly

steps.detail: Console Settings > enable Multi DC if your users span data centers; each DC has its own unique client secret, which you must store and select correctly.
steps.title: (Optional) Enable Multi-DC

tagline: Open, self-service OAuth with no client approval at all, but the operational model is the work: per-data-center endpoints and secrets, organization-scoped grants, a 20-refresh-token cap that silently invalidates the oldest, and a grant-token lifetime Zoho's own docs state three different ways.

time.active: ~5 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of DC-aware flow code
time.total: Same day; no approval wait exists
